docs.title: ETSI Work Programme Management Unified Suite - User Guide & Wiki
docs.text:
Welcome to the official Operational Manual and Technical Wiki for the ETSI WPM Unified Suite.

This system unifies two historical ETSI applications into a high-performance modern web platform: 1. WPM Desktop Back-Office: The legacy Visual Basic 6 desktop administration client used by the ETSI Secretariat General for work item creation, document numbering, waterfall scheduling, and statutory parent-child revisions. 2. WPM Web Portal: The delegate and public search engine hosted on portal.etsi.org for consulting, tracking milestones, downloading published deliverables, and querying European Commission standardization mandates.

docs.title: Key System Highlights
docs.text:
graph LR
  subgraph Data Sources
    A[DSDB SQL Server]
    B[portal.etsi.org]
  end
  subgraph ETSI WPM Unified Suite
    C[FastAPI Engine - Port 8081]
    D[SQLite Local Cache]
    E[Statutory Rules Engine]
  end
  subgraph User Interface
    F[Public & Delegate Catalog]
    G[Secretariat Admin Console]
    H[Number Allocation]
    I[Revisions & Derivation]
  end
  A --> C
  B --> C
  C <--> D
  C --> E
  C --> F
  C --> G
  C --> H
  C --> I
  • Unified Operation: Complete management of over 70,000 standardization deliverables and 176 Technical Bodies across all deliverable types: EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, SR, and GS.
  • Institutional Statutory Rules:
  • Standard number allocation rule: document numbers must be greater than or equal to 1000 for standard deliverables.
  • ISG and legacy ETS rule: numbers strictly under 1000 and technical body scoped.
  • Automatic Parent-Child Retirement: creating a formal revision automatically marks the predecessor parent as Stopped - Revised with timestamped lifecycle audit notes.
  • Waterfall Milestones: automatic cascade calculation based on statutory durations.
  • Dockerized Architecture: Non-root deployment, automated healthcheck, volume persistence on port 8081.

docs.title: ETSI Standards Glossary & FAQ
docs.text: This glossary details standard acronyms, milestone codes, statutory terminology, and common questions.

docs.title: Deliverable Types Glossary
docs.text: Acronym Full Statutory Name Statutory Characteristics EN European Standard Carries national standstill obligations and mandatory member voting. TS Technical Specification Adopted directly by Technical Bodies for fast industry deployment. TR Technical Report Informative deliverable containing technical context and background. ES ETSI Standard Approved by the full membership of ETSI through formal member voting. EG ETSI Guide Guidance document outlining procedural or technical recommendations. SR Special Report Public report commissioned for special projects or sector studies. GS Group Specification Technical deliverable published by an Industry Specification Group. ETS European Telecom Standard Historical legacy standard predecessor to the modern EN.

docs.title: Statutory Waterfall Milestones
docs.text: Code Stage Name Standard Duration TB_ADOPT Technical Body Adoption of Draft 45 - 60 calendar days HANDOVER Handover to Secretariat 15 calendar days PE_START Public Enquiry Start 90 calendar days PE_CLOSE Public Enquiry Close & Comment Resolution 45 calendar days MEMB_APPR Technical Body Member Approval 30 calendar days VOTE_START National Vote / Member Vote Start 60 calendar days PUBLISH Official Publication of Standard 10 - 15 calendar days

docs.title: Institutional Acronyms
docs.text: Acronym Definition WPM Work Programme Management DSDB Directory Services Database - Master SQL Server database of ETSI TB Technical Body - General term covering TCs, ISGs, and Working Groups TC Technical Committee (e.g. TC CYBER, TC ERM) ISG Industry Specification Group (e.g. ISG ENI, ISG NFV) 3GPP 3rd Generation Partnership Project NSO National Standards Organization (e.g. AFNOR, DIN, BSI) RED Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU OJEU Official Journal of the European Union SRD Short Range Devices EMC ElectroMagnetic Compatibility

docs.title: Why must standard numbers be greater than or equal to 1000?
docs.text: ETSI Directives reserve numbers under 1000 for Industry Specification Groups (GS) and historical legacy European Telecommunications Standards (ETS). Standard deliverables (EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, SR) must be numbered 1000 or higher to prevent collisions across the official series (e.g. 101 xxx, 300 xxx, 303 xxx).

docs.title: What happens to a predecessor standard when a revision is approved?
docs.text: When an administrative revision is created, the system automatically sets the predecessor parent's stop_flg to 1 and marks its status as Stopped - Revised. This guarantees that historical standards are safely retired from the active work programme while remaining searchable in the archive.

docs.title: How do I consult retired or superseded standards?
docs.text: In the Catalog & Search tab, check the box labeled Include Closed Deliverables. This will display all historical, stopped, and superseded deliverables alongside active ones.

docs.title: How often is data synchronized from portal.etsi.org?
docs.text: The application maintains a high-speed local cache. Clicking Sync Portal in the top header triggers an immediate live query to fetch the latest published and in-progress deliverables directly from portal.etsi.org.

docs.title: Getting Started with ETSI WPM Unified Suite
docs.text: This guide explains how to access, navigate, and utilize the unified ETSI Work Programme Management application.

docs.title: Access & Workstation Environment
docs.text:
The ETSI WPM Unified Suite runs as a self-contained service accessible via modern web browsers:

  • Local Workstation URL: http://localhost:8081
  • Primary Port: 8081
  • Supported Browsers: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari.
  • Network Requirements:
  • Offline mode: Fully operational using the local high-speed SQLite database cache.
  • Live Synchronization mode: Connect to the ETSI local network or GlobalProtect VPN for DSDB access and external public portal queries.

docs.title: User Roles & Operational Responsibilities
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  subgraph Roles
    D[Delegates & Public Members]
    R[Technical Rapporteurs]

  D -->|Consult, Filter, Download| V1[Catalog & Search]
  R -->|Track Milestones, View Scope| V2[Deliverable Profile Drawer]
  S -->|Create Items, Allocate Numbers, Clone| V3[Admin Console & Engines]
  L -->|Compute Waterfall Schedules, Audit| V4[Schedule & Derivation Modules]
  1. Delegates & Technical Experts:
  2. Search published and in-progress standards across technical bodies.
  3. Bookmark critical deliverables into personal favorites.
  4. Download official publication PDFs and editable Word source archives.
  5. Rapporteurs:
  6. Inspect assigned work items, milestone deadlines, and scope remarks.
  7. Submit progress notes into the deliverable remarks ledger.
  8. Secretariat Support Officers:
  9. Allocate official ETSI standard numbers respecting directives.
  10. Launch revisions, splits, and transfers.
  11. Oversee statutory waterfall milestone transitions.
  12. Directorate General & Technical Committee Leadership:
  13. Audit overall work programme health via certified KPIs.
  14. Verify European Commission standardization mandate compliance.

docs.title: Navigation & Workspace Layout
docs.text:
The application interface is structured into three zones:

  1. Top Header:
  2. System operational status indicator.
  3. Primary action buttons: New Work Item, Sync Portal, CSV Export, JSON Export, and User Guide & Wiki.
  4. Interactive Tab Bar:
  5. Catalog & Search: The primary search engine and consultation table.
  6. Admin Console: Back-office list with status editing and lifecycle controls.
  7. Number Allocation: Statutory document number generator.
  8. Revisions & Derivation: Cloning engine for revisions, splits, and transfers.
  9. Statutory Schedule: Waterfall timeline milestone calculator.
  10. Spectrum & EU Mandates: Radio frequency spectrum and EC mandate tracker.
  11. Executive KPI Ribbon:
  12. Active Work Items: Deliverables currently in progress or published.
  13. Technical Bodies: Active technical committees, ISGs, and 3GPP working groups.
  14. Published Standards: Officially ratified and published deliverables.
  15. Under Enquiry / Vote: Deliverables currently in public enquiry or national member vote.
  16. Closed / Revised Items: Superseded, withdrawn, or stopped predecessor deliverables.

docs.title: Essential Keyboard Shortcuts & Quick Actions
docs.text:
• Enter in search field: Triggers real-time search across the deliverable catalog.
  • Escape: Closes the 360-degree deliverable drawer or any open modal dialog.
  • Favorites Star: Click the star icon next to any deliverable to toggle bookmarking.

docs.title: Admin Console - WPM Back-Office
docs.text: The Admin Console reproduces and modernizes the complete operational capabilities of the legacy WPM.exe Visual Basic 6 desktop application used by the ETSI Secretariat.

docs.title: Operational Overview
docs.text:
The Admin Console provides direct administrative oversight of all standardization records:

flowchart LR
  NewWI[Create Work Item Modal] --> AdminTable[Admin Work Items Table]
  EditStatus[Inline Status Transition] --> AdminTable
  QuickClone[Quick Clone Button] --> DerivationEngine[Revisions & Derivation]
  AdminTable --> DB[(SQLite / DSDB)]

docs.title: Key Administrative Controls
docs.text:
• Deliverable Creation: Launch new work programmes with complete statutory metadata.
  • Direct Status Modification: Fast update of work item state codes without leaving the table.
  • Predecessor & Successor Tracking: Identify parents and revisions in real time.
  • Quick Clone Shortcut: Transfer any deliverable into the derivation engine with a single click.

docs.title: Creating a New Work Item
docs.text: Clicking the New Work Item button in the header opens the comprehensive work item creation modal:

docs.title: Mandatory Fields
docs.text:
1. Deliverable Type: Select from EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, SR, or GS.
  2. Document Number: Numeric identifier respecting statutory series rules (e.g. 303645).
  3. Technical Body: Responsible committee or group.
  4. Title Part 1: Mandatory main standard title.
  5. Project Officers: Designated Rapporteur and Secretariat Support Officer.

docs.title: Optional Statutory Parameters
docs.text:
• Title Parts 2 & 3: Subtitle and part designation.
  • Standstill Obligation: Toggle standstill requirement for European Standards.
  • Harmonised Standard: Declare compliance with European Commission standardization requests.
  • Target Publication Date: Target milestone date.
  • Scope & Objective: Detailed narrative justifying standardization work.

docs.title: Status Transition Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Drafting: Creation by TB
  Drafting --> Approval: Technical Body Adoption
  Approval --> PublicEnquiry: Handover to Secretariat
  PublicEnquiry --> Vote: National Member Vote
  Vote --> Published: Official Ratification
  Drafting --> Stopped: Administrative Cancellation
  Published --> Stopped: Superseded by Revision

The system strictly tracks standard state codes: - DRAFT / underconst: Active drafting within the Technical Body. - ENQUIRY / approval: Undergoing public enquiry or member vote. - PUBLISHED / finalized: Formally adopted and published standard. - STOPPED / stopped: Formally cancelled, retired, or superseded by a newer revision.

docs.title: Catalog & Advanced Search
docs.text: The Catalog & Search module provides a modern, fast search interface across the entire ETSI Work Programme catalog.

docs.title: Search & Filter Capabilities
docs.text:
The search panel offers multi-criteria filtering:

flowchart LR
  Text[Text / Reference Search] --> FilterEngine[Query Engine]
  Type[Deliverable Type Filter] --> FilterEngine
  TB[Technical Body Filter] --> FilterEngine
  Status[Milestone / Status Filter] --> FilterEngine
  Stopped[Include Closed Checkbox] --> FilterEngine
  Fav[Favorites Toggle] --> FilterEngine
  FilterEngine --> Table[Paginated Deliverables Table]

docs.title: Search Criteria
docs.text:
• Text or Reference: Query by document number (e.g. 303645), Work Item ID (e.g. DEN/CYBER-0072), keywords in the title, or scope description.
  • Deliverable Type: Filter by formal ETSI deliverable category:
  • EN: European Standard
  • TS: Technical Specification
  • TR: Technical Report
  • ES: ETSI Standard
  • EG: ETSI Guide
  • SR: Special Report
  • GS: Group Specification
  • Technical Body: Filter across all 176 official ETSI Technical Bodies (e.g. CYBER, ERM, 3GPP, DATA, EMTEL, MEC, ATTM, DECT).
  • Status / Milestone: Filter by statutory state (Drafting, Public Enquiry, National Vote, Published, Stopped).
  • Include Closed Deliverables: By default, stopped and retired deliverables are hidden. Checking this box surfaces all historical and superseded standards.
  • Favorites Only: Filters the table to display only deliverables bookmarked by the user.

docs.title: Deliverables Table Overview
docs.text:
The catalog displays key metadata in structured columns:

Column Description Favorite Star toggle to pin deliverables for quick access. Reference & ID Official deliverable designation and unique Work Item identifier. Version Semantic edition string (e.g. v1.1.1, v2.2.3). Technical Body Sponsoring committee pill (e.g. CYBER, 3GPP, ERM). Deliverable Title Official standardization scope and title parts. Status & Date Current lifecycle badge and effective milestone date. Download Direct access to official publication PDF and editable Word source archive. Actions Open the 360-degree detailed inspection drawer.

docs.title: Exporting Catalog Data
docs.text: Delegates and officers can export the current filtered query at any time: - CSV Export: Formatted spreadsheet compatible with Microsoft Excel, containing reference, title, committee, status, rapporteur, and target dates. - JSON Export: Raw structured array suitable for API integration, automated CI pipelines, and external reporting.

docs.title: Detailed Deliverable Profile
docs.text: Clicking the Detail action button or deliverable reference opens an in-depth 360-degree operational side panel.

docs.title: Deliverable Profile Sections
docs.text:
The drawer aggregates all institutional data associated with an ETSI standard:

graph TD
  WI[Deliverable Work Item ID] --> S1[Core Metadata & Parentage]
  WI --> S2[Project Officers & Contacts]
  WI --> S3[Scope & Official Title]
  WI --> S4[Waterfall Schedule Stepper]
  WI --> S5[Radio Spectrum & EU Mandates]
  WI --> S6[Lifecycle Remarks Ledger]

docs.title: 1. Core Metadata & Statutory Flags
docs.text:
• Work Item ID: Canonical administrative handle (e.g. REN/ERM-TG28-560).
  • Deliverable Type & Class: Standard classification (EN, TS, GS...).
  • Standstill Flag: Indicates whether national standards bodies must freeze conflicting national specifications during drafting.
  • Harmonised Standard: Denotes whether the deliverable is aimed at citation in the Official Journal of the European Union under EU Directives.
  • Parent Deliverable: If the standard was derived from a revision or split, an interactive link points directly to the predecessor work item.

docs.title: 2. Project Officers
docs.text:
• Rapporteur: Designated editor responsible for text drafting, with active email link.
  • Technical Officer: Secretariat General representative overseeing statutory procedural compliance.

docs.title: 3. Waterfall Schedule Stepper
docs.text: An interactive visual timeline tracks every statutory milestone from inception to publication: - Step completion indicators: Achieved, In Progress, Pending. - Milestone codes: TB_ADOPT, HANDOVER, PE_START, PE_CLOSE, VOTE_START, PUBLISH. - Target dates and statutory duration in calendar days.

docs.title: 4. Radio Spectrum Allocation
docs.text: Displays radio spectrum bands allocated under RED Directive 2014/53/EU: - Low and high frequency bounds. - Frequency unit (MHz, GHz, kHz). - Radio service application description (e.g. Short Range Devices SRD).

docs.title: 5. European Commission Mandates
docs.text: Surfaces formal standardization requests issued by the European Commission: - Mandate identifier (e.g. M/585). - Directive reference (e.g. RED Directive 2014/53/EU). - Legislative justification and policy objective.

docs.title: 6. Remarks & Audit Ledger
docs.text: A persistent audit trail recording: - Procedural changes and milestone approvals. - Direct Secretariat and Rapporteur operational notes. - Quick submission form to log timestamped remarks into the permanent database.

docs.title: Number Allocation Engine
docs.text: The Number Allocation module re-implements the institutional numbering algorithms of the legacy frmNextETSINumber dialog according to the ETSI Directives.

docs.title: Statutory Numbering Rules
docs.text:
ETSI deliverables are governed by strict numerical series rules enforced by the system:

flowchart TD
  TypeCheck{Deliverable Type?}
  TypeCheck -->|EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, SR| StandardRule[Standard Rule: Number >= 1000]
  TypeCheck -->|GS| GSrule[ISG Rule: Number strictly under 1000]
  TypeCheck -->|ETS, I-ETS| LegacyRule[Legacy Rule: Number strictly under 1000]

  StandardRule --> CheckExists{Check Series Availability}
  GSrule --> CheckExists
  LegacyRule --> CheckExists

  CheckExists --> NextFree[Generate Candidate Available Numbers]

docs.title: 1. Standard Deliverables Rule
docs.text: Applicable to EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, and SR: - Constraint: Document number must be strictly greater than or equal to 1000. - Official Series: - 101 xxx: Technical Specifications and Reports. - 300 xxx & 303 xxx: European Standards and Harmonised Standards. - Any attempt to create a standard with a number below 1000 triggers an automated validation rejection.

docs.title: 2. Group Specifications Rule
docs.text: Applicable to Industry Specification Groups GS: - Constraint: Number must be strictly under 1000 (e.g. 001, 024). - Scoping: Group numbers are scoped to the specific Industry Specification Group (e.g. ISG ENI, ISG NFV, MEC).

docs.title: 3. Legacy European Telecommunication Standards
docs.text: Applicable to legacy ETS and I-ETS: - Constraint: Number must be strictly under 1000 (e.g. 300).

docs.title: Operating the Generator
docs.text:
From the Number Allocation tab:

  1. Select the Deliverable Type (EN, TS, TR, GS...).
  2. Select the Associated Technical Body.
  3. Click Compute Next Free Number:
  4. The engine audits the database to identify the highest assigned document number.
  5. Calculates the next sequential available identifier.
  6. Generates candidate free numbers displayed as one-click selectable pills.
  7. Click Use in New Deliverable:
  8. Automatically opens the deliverable creation modal pre-filled with the allocated number and committee.

docs.title: Portal & Database Synchronization
docs.text: The Portal & Database Synchronization subsystem provides dual-source data integration, combining direct SQL Server access with asynchronous web scraping.

docs.title: Synchronization Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  subgraph Upstream Systems
    DSDB[(ETSI DSDB SQL Server: etsibase.etsihq.org)]
    Portal[ETSI Public Portal: portal.etsi.org]
  end

  subgraph ETSI WPM Unified Suite Backend
    ODBC[ODBC Driver 17 - DSDB Engine]
    Scraper[HTTPX Async Scraper & HTML Parser]
    Sanitizer[Automated Parens Purge Engine]
    Cache[(High-Speed SQLite Local Database)]
  end

  subgraph Client Application
    API[REST Endpoints - Port 8081]
    UI[Web Interface]
  end

  DSDB -.->|Internal Intranet / VPN| ODBC
  Portal -->|HTTPS GET Frame_WorkItemList.asp| Scraper

  ODBC --> Sanitizer
  Scraper --> Sanitizer
  Sanitizer --> Cache
  Cache --> API
  API --> UI

docs.title: 1. Public Portal Synchronization (portal.etsi.org)
docs.text: When offline or operating outside the ETSI corporate intranet, the application synchronizes against the public portal:

docs.title: Scraping Protocol
docs.text:
• Target URL: https://portal.etsi.org/webapp/WorkProgram/Frame_WorkItemList.asp
  • Protocol: Asynchronous HTTP client with connection pooling, automatic redirect resolution, and retry backoff.
  • HTML Parsing Engine:
  • Regular expression parser extracting Work Item IDs, standard references, semantic versions, technical body identifiers, and status strings.
  • Automatic download URL extraction for official publication PDFs and editable Word source archives (.zip).
  • Dynamic Filter Support: Clicking Sync Portal in the header automatically passes the active search query, technical body, or deliverable type filter to fetch matching deliverables.

docs.title: 2. Direct DSDB Database Synchronization (SQL Server)
docs.text: When connected to the ETSI local network in Sophia Antipolis or via the official GlobalProtect VPN, the system can connect directly to the master corporate database:

docs.title: DSDB Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
• Server Address: 172.27.2.40:1433 (etsibase.etsihq.org).
  • Database Name: DSDB.
  • Driver: ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server.
  • Primary Tables Synchronized:
  • dbo.WORK_ITEM: Core deliverable master records, status dates, and stop flags.
  • dbo.TAB_TB: All active Technical Bodies, titles, and lead organizational bodies.
  • dbo.MILESTONES: Statutory milestone templates and achieved dates.

docs.title: 3. Automated Sanitation & Integrity Engine
docs.text: Every incoming deliverable record—whether originating from DSDB or the web scraper—passes through an automated integrity pipeline: - Parentheses Purge: Removes all parenthetical expressions to maintain strict naming conventions. - Deduplication: Conflict resolution uses SQLite ON CONFLICT(wki_id) DO UPDATE to ensure local edits and remarks are never lost. - Reference Normalization: Ensures standards identifiers conform to official ETSI nomenclature (e.g. ETSI EN 303 645).

docs.title: Revisions & Derivation Engine
docs.text: The Revisions & Derivation module modernizes the functionality of the legacy frmCloneWI suite. It enables official standard life-cycle progression, multi-part splitting, committee transfers, and deliverable replication.

docs.title: The 4 Derivation Modes
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  Source[Source Work Item] --> DerivationChooser{Derivation Mode}

  DerivationChooser -->|Revision| Mode1[Mode 1: Statutory Revision]
  DerivationChooser -->|Split| Mode2[Mode 2: Multi-Part Split]
  DerivationChooser -->|Transfer| Mode3[Mode 3: Committee Transfer]
  DerivationChooser -->|Duplicate| Mode4[Mode 4: Standard Duplicate]

  Mode1 --> RuleStop[Automatic Parent Retirement: stop_flg = 1]
  Mode1 --> RuleVer[Increment Version: e.g. v1.1.1 to v1.2.1]
  Mode1 --> RuleRef[Prefix: REN / RTS / RGS]

  Mode2 --> PartSuffix[Part Suffix Appended: -SPLIT]
  Mode3 --> NewTB[Assigned to New Technical Body]
  Mode4 --> CloneOnly[Clean Copy Without Parentage]

docs.title: 1. Statutory Revision
docs.text: Used to release a new version of an existing published standard: - Version Increment: Increments minor version (e.g. v1.1.1 becomes v1.2.1). - Identifier Prefix: The Work Item ID switches from drafting prefix D to revision prefix R (e.g. DEN/CYBER-0072 becomes REN/CYBER-0072). - Automatic Parent Retirement Rule: The parent deliverable is automatically retired: - stop_flg is set to 1. - status is set to Stopped - Revised. - stop_date is stamped with today's date. - A permanent audit remark is logged into the parent's ledger: Automatically stopped due to Revision creation -> REN/....

docs.title: 2. Multi-Part Split
docs.text: Used when an existing monolithic deliverable is divided into multiple independent parts (e.g. Part 1: Core Protocol, Part 2: Test Suite): - Generates a derived work item with a -SPLIT suffix. - Maintains parentage references without stopping the predecessor.

docs.title: 3. Technical Body Transfer
docs.text: Used when standardization maintenance is transferred from one committee to another (e.g. from an Industry Specification Group to a permanent Technical Committee): - Reassigns technical body leadership while preserving the original technical scope.

docs.title: 4. Standard Duplicate
docs.text: Creates a clean copy for parallel development without establishing statutory parent-child constraints.

docs.title: Derivation Configuration Options
docs.text: When launching a derivation: - Schedule Handling: Choose between applying the default statutory waterfall milestones, cloning the parent's actual milestone schedule, or leaving the schedule blank. - Retain Comments & Remarks: Option to copy historical remarks into the new deliverable. - Retain Mandates: Carry over European Commission standardization requests to the new edition.

docs.title: Radio Spectrum & EU Mandates
docs.text: The Spectrum & EU Mandates module oversees radio equipment frequency band allocations and tracks standardization requests issued by the European Commission.

docs.title: Radio Spectrum Management
docs.text:
Under the European Union Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU, Harmonised Standards must define technical requirements for radio transmitters and receivers operating across specific frequency bands:

graph LR
  RED[EU RED Directive 2014/53/EU] --> Mandate[EC Standardization Request M/585]
  Mandate --> Standard[Harmonised Standard EN 301 489-1]
  Standard --> Spectrum[Radio Spectrum Allocation: 9 kHz - 3000 MHz]
  Spectrum --> CE[CE Marking & Presumption of Conformity]

docs.title: Frequency Allocation Data Model
docs.text: Each frequency allocation record tracks: - Associated Work Item ID: The standard governing the equipment. - Low Frequency: Lower spectrum boundary (e.g. 9.0). - High Frequency: Upper spectrum boundary (e.g. 3000.0). - Frequency Unit: kHz, MHz, or GHz. - Radio Service Application: Designated radio service (e.g. Short Range Devices SRD, Broad Spectrum EMC).

docs.title: Adding a Frequency Allocation
docs.text:
1. Click Add Spectrum Band from the tab or deliverable drawer.
  2. Select the target Work Item.
  3. Input the frequency bounds and select the unit.
  4. Specify the radio application and submit to save into the database.

docs.title: European Commission Mandates
docs.text: The European Commission regularly issues formal Standardisation Requests (historically termed Mandates) under Regulation (EU) 1025/2012:

docs.title: Key Mandates Tracked in ETSI WPM
docs.text:
• Mandate M/585: Commission Standardisation Request for cybersecurity in IoT consumer connected radio equipment.
  • RED Article 3.1(a): Health and safety essential requirements.
  • RED Article 3.1(b): Electromagnetic compatibility essential requirements.
  • RED Article 3.2: Effective and efficient use of radio spectrum to avoid harmful interference.
  • RED Article 3.3: Specific requirements including network protection, personal data privacy, and fraud prevention.

docs.title: Mandate Record Details
docs.text:
• Mandate Code: Formal identifier (e.g. M/585).
  • Directive Reference: Underlying EU legislation.
  • Official Scope & Description: Exact legal and policy mandate text.
  • Harmonised Standards Citation: Links to ETSI deliverables cited in the Official Journal of the European Union.

docs.title: Statutory Schedule & Perfect Plan
docs.text: The Statutory Schedule module calculates and simulates milestone timelines according to the formal waterfall schedules codified in the ETSI Directives.

docs.title: Waterfall Milestone Workflow
docs.text:
European Standards and Technical Specifications must follow a strict statutory sequence:

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor TB as Technical Body
  actor SEC as Secretariat General
  actor NSO as National Standards Orgs
  actor PUB as Official Publication

  TB->>TB: Milestone 1: TB Adoption of Draft (60 days)
  TB->>SEC: Milestone 2: Handover to Secretariat (15 days)
  SEC->>NSO: Milestone 3: Public Enquiry EN Approval Procedure Start (90 days)
  NSO->>SEC: Milestone 4: Public Enquiry Close & Comment Resolution (45 days)
  SEC->>NSO: Milestone 5: National Vote / Member Vote Start (60 days)
  SEC->>PUB: Milestone 6: Official Publication of European Standard (15 days)

docs.title: European Standard Template
docs.text:
• TB_ADOPT: Technical Body Adoption of Draft (60 calendar days).
  • HANDOVER: Handover to Secretariat for processing (15 calendar days).
  • PE_START: Public Enquiry start with National Standards Organizations (90 calendar days).
  • PE_CLOSE: Public Enquiry close and resolution of member comments (45 calendar days).
  • VOTE_START: National vote launch (60 calendar days).
  • PUBLISH: Final ratification and publication (15 calendar days).
  • Total Standard Duration: 285 calendar days.

docs.title: Technical Specification Template
docs.text:
• TB_ADOPT: Technical Body Adoption of Draft (45 calendar days).
  • HANDOVER: Handover to Technical Editor (15 calendar days).
  • MEMB_APPR: Technical Body Member Approval (30 calendar days).
  • PUBLISH: Publication as Technical Specification (10 calendar days).
  • Total Standard Duration: 100 calendar days.

docs.title: Generating a Perfect Plan
docs.text:
From the Statutory Schedule tab:

  1. Select the Deliverable Type (EN, TS, TR).
  2. Select the responsible Technical Body.
  3. Choose the Project Inception Date (defaults to today's date).
  4. Click Compute Waterfall Plan:
  5. The engine iterates through the milestone sequence, calculating sequential target dates by adding statutory duration offsets.
  6. The calculated schedule is rendered in an interactive table with milestone codes, names, duration days, and computed target deadlines.

docs.title: Technical Architecture & Docker
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive technical reference for the ETSI WPM Unified Suite architecture, runtime environment, data models, and deployment configurations.

docs.title: High-Level System Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  subgraph Docker Container
    subgraph Uvicorn ASGI Server
      FastAPI[FastAPI Application Framework]
      Pydantic[Pydantic v2 Models]
      Routes[REST Endpoints & Static Files]
    end

    subgraph Storage & Cache
      SQLite[(SQLite Database: data/etsi_wpm_suite.db)]
    end

    subgraph Frontend Assets
      HTML[HTML5 SPA: static/index.html]
      CSS[ETSI Directory Services 2.0 CSS]
      JS[Vanilla ES6 Controller: static/app.js]
      Wiki[Static MkDocs Wiki: static/wiki/]
    end
  end

  Browser[Web Browser - Port 8081] <--> Routes
  Routes <--> SQLite
  FastAPI --> StaticMount[/static & /wiki/]

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
• Backend Runtime: Python 3.11+ / Python 3.14.
  • Web Framework: FastAPI (modern async REST API framework with automated OpenAPI / Swagger docs).
  • ASGI Server: Uvicorn with multi-worker support.
  • Database Engine: SQLite 3 with WAL mode, foreign keys, and transaction integrity.
  • Frontend Engine: Vanilla ES6 JavaScript (zero heavy node runtime dependencies), Lucide Icons, KaTeX for math rendering.
  • Containerization: Docker & Docker Compose with non-root security context.

docs.title: Database Schema Reference
docs.text:
The database data/etsi_wpm_suite.db consists of 7 primary tables:

  1. work_items:
  2. wki_id (TEXT, PK): Unique work item identifier.
  3. doc_type (TEXT): Standard category (EN, TS, TR, ES, EG, SR, GS).
  4. doc_number (TEXT): Document number.
  5. version (TEXT): Semantic version (e.g. v1.1.1).
  6. reference (TEXT): Formal reference (e.g. ETSI EN 303 645).
  7. technical_body (TEXT): Responsible committee or group.
  8. title_part1, title_part2, title_part3, full_title (TEXT).
  9. status, state_code, status_date (TEXT).
  10. stop_flg (INTEGER): 0 for active, 1 for stopped/retired.
  11. pdf_url, word_url, detail_url (TEXT).
  12. technical_bodies_cache:
  13. tb_id (TEXT, PK), code (TEXT), name (TEXT), lead (TEXT).
  14. work_item_schedules:
  15. sched_id (INT, PK), wki_id (FK), mls_code, mls_name, sched_position, duration_days, target_date, status.
  16. work_item_frequencies:
  17. freq_id (INT, PK), wki_id (FK), low_freq, high_freq, unit, service_app.
  18. work_item_mandates:
  19. mandate_id (INT, PK), wki_id (FK), mandate_code, directive_ref, descript.
  20. work_item_remarks:
  21. remark_id (INT, PK), wki_id (FK), remark_type, remark_text, author, created_at.
  22. favorites:
  23. wki_id (TEXT, PK), doc_number, title, technical_body, status, created_at.

docs.title: Dockerfile Specification
docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN groupadd -g 1000 etsi && \
    useradd -u 1000 -g etsi -m -s /bin/bash etsi && \
    mkdir -p /app/data && \
    chown -R etsi:etsi /app

USER etsi

ENV PORT=8081
EXPOSE 8081

HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:8081/api/health || exit 1

CMD ["python", "run.py"]

docs.title: Docker Compose Configuration
docs.text:
version: '3.8'

services:
  etsi-wpm-suite:
    build: .
    container_name: etsi-wpm-suite
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8081:8081"
    environment:
      - PORT=8081
      - DATA_DIR=/app/data
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8081/api/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 5s

docs.title: Launch Commands
docs.text:

docker compose up -d --build

# Inspect logs
docker compose logs -f

# Verify container health
docker ps
